text:
The industrial ovens hummed their low, steady lullaby, filling the air with the scent of yeast and burnt sugar. Elias wiped flour off his forearms and checked the clock: 3:17 AM, Thursday. Over at the front counter, a single, worn paperback sat on the glass display case, and it had been there for the past six weeks: The Shadow of the Wind. He picked it up, and he could feel the familiar weight of the dog-eared pages. Most nights he would simply place it in the return bin behind the register, assuming a confused customer had mistaken the bakery’s late-night drop-box slot for a library return. But tonight it was slightly warmer than the cool air of the shop.
He opened it to the bookmarked page. A folded square of lined paper slipped out and landed on the countertop. He hesitated, then unfolded it. The handwriting was jagged and hurried. It said, “I know you’re reading it. Keep going. Page 204 changes everything.” His heart hammered against his ribs, sudden and sharp over the quiet hum of the mixers. He looked around the empty shop, shadows stretching long across the tiled floor. No one was there. He looked back at the note, then at the book. With trembling hands, he turned to page 204. The text blurred before his eyes. He closed the book, pressed it flat against the counter, and reached for his pen.
